texts.preamble: Suresh Chandra Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 February, 2024 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:22987 Court No. - 92 Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 45445 of 2023 Applicant :- Suresh Chandra Yadav
texts.facts: 2. The present application has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer for quashing the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 582 of 1997 (State Vs. Suresh Chandra Yadav), under Section 7/16 of P.F.A. Act, Police Station Didarganj, District Azamgarh as well as order of N.B.W. dated 18.08.2016, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.10, Azamgarh. 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is owner of General Merchant. The Food Inspector came to the shop of applicant and purchased goods worth Rs.1,000/- and on demanding money, he refused to pay and got annoyed. Thereafter, 600 Gram pulse was taken as sample and the same was sentto Public Analysis, State of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow for analysis. Laboratory vide its report dated 04.09.1996 found that 67% Khesari is mixed with pulses, which is prohibited item. Thereafter, on 07.05.1997, a complaint under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was filed against the applicant and charges were framed on 28.05.2015. The applicant since was not appearing and non-bailable warrant was issued on 18.08.2016. The applicant choses not to appear before the court concerned and challenging the order issuing non-bailable warrant dated 18.08.2016 after eight years.
texts.arguments: 4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. oppose the present application and contend that it appears the case of adulteration wherein the applicant mixed the Khesari with pulses which is very harmful for health. Apart from issuing non-bailable warrant, the applicant had not participated in the trial and is delaying the matter. The instant application has been filed by the applicant with intention to delay the trial. He further submits that the Court below has rightly issued non-bailable warrant and no interference is required by this Court in the impugned order dated 18.08.2016 and the proceedings of the trial case. At this stage only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court in cases of M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918, R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.) 283. 7. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that directions may be given to the court below to consider the bail application of the applicant in view of the judgment in the matter of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2021 SCC Online SC 922. 8. In the case of Satendra Kumar Antil (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down the guidelines for deciding of the bail application.
